canonical_topic: Nuclear weapon proliferation risk from enrichment process
definition: The enrichment process used to produce civilian reactor fuel is nearly identical to the process used to produce weapons-grade material, creating a dual-use policy challenge.
core_idea: Ensuring a reliable civilian nuclear fuel supply while preventing that same enrichment capability from being diverted to weapons production is described as an ongoing public-policy challenge.
key_points: The enrichment process for civilian fuel and for nuclear weapons fuel is nearly identical.
Guaranteeing civilian fuel supply without enabling military diversion is characterized as a persistent public-policy problem.
relationships: Directly tied to the enrichment-percentage contrast (4% vs 90%+) described earlier in the chapter.
trading_implications: Proliferation policy constraints on enrichment capacity are a structural risk factor for uranium fuel supply chains.
